Logistics / Courier & last-mile delivery

More first-attempt deliveries, fewer returns, faster COD.

For express couriers, e-commerce last-mile networks, hyperlocal fleets and regional delivery partners. We connect merchant bookings, rider onboarding, tracking, failed-delivery handling and COD settlement, so branches act on exceptions the same day and merchants and consignees hear from you before they call.

The challenge

What makes courier & last-mile delivery different.

01

Failed deliveries are recorded with vague or questionable reason codes and turn into return-to-origin costs for merchants and the network.

02

Merchants and consignees call branches for pickup and delivery status because updates are late or generic.

03

COD cash passes through riders, branches, banks and UPI before remittance, and reconciliation runs on spreadsheets.

04

High rider turnover means constant onboarding, with licenses, vehicle papers and verification tracked by hand.

05

Pickups booked after cut-off or with wrong weights lead to missed pickups and billing disputes.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for courier & last-mile delivery.

01

Pickup booking on WhatsApp and the portal

Merchants book pickups through a WhatsApp Flow, the portal or an API, with serviceability, restricted-item and weight checks before a slot is confirmed.

02

NDR resolution with consignee choices

Consignees confirm or correct the failure reason and choose a re-attempt date, landmark, alternate contact or pickup point, written back before the next dispatch plan.

03

Proactive delay updates

Shipments that stall at a hub or miss their promised date get an owner and a consignee update before the first complaint.

04

COD reconciliation and merchant remittances

Rider collections, branch deposits and UPI settlements are matched to AWBs daily, and remittance files with statements are prepared for finance to release.

05

Rider onboarding and document expiry tracking

License, registration, insurance and PUC are collected with consent, verified and tracked to expiry, so riders with lapsed documents are not assigned.

06

Where-is-my-parcel assistant

Consignees and merchants get answers from live tracking on WhatsApp, with handover to an agent for claims, damage and refunds.

Booking & pickup requestStandard4–6 weeks

Booking and pickup scheduling on WhatsApp and the portal

Let merchants book pickups through a WhatsApp Flow, the portal or an API, check serviceability, restricted items and weight before accepting, assign a pickup slot by branch cut-off, and confirm with the AWB, labels and a reminder.

Courier & last-mile delivery

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Small merchants book pickups by calling or messaging a branch, often after the daily cut-off, with incomplete addresses, wrong weights or unserviceable pin codes. Riders arrive to find parcels unpacked or not ready, missed pickups go unexplained to the merchant, and weight disputes surface later at billing.

Trigger

A merchant completes the WhatsApp booking Flow, creates a shipment in the portal, or pushes orders through the API or a connected seller platform.

How it runs

  • Capture pickup address, ready time, number of packages, declared weight and dimensions, payment mode and declared value through a WhatsApp Flow, portal form or API.
  • Check pin code serviceability, COD limits, prohibited and restricted items, and whether the declared value needs an e-way bill number before pickup.
  • Create the shipment and AWB in the courier TMS, assign a pickup slot by branch cut-off and rider route, and send the merchant a confirmation with labels.
  • Remind the merchant before the slot, and alert the branch when a rider is running late or a pickup is at risk of being missed.
  • Record pickup scans and measured weight; when it differs from the declared weight beyond the agreed tolerance, attach dimensioner photos and notify the merchant.
  • Send failed pickups to the branch supervisor with the reason, and offer the merchant the next available slot.

Human checkpoint

Branch supervisors approve exceptions such as pickups after cut-off, restricted items and high-value or bulk pickups. Weight disputes are decided by the billing team using the photos and dimension records, never by the automation.

Systems it connects

  • Courier TMS or last-mile platform
  • Rider app
  • Seller platforms such as Shopify or Unicommerce
  • Pin code serviceability master
  • E-way bill system via GSP

Data & consent

Uses merchant business details, pickup addresses and the consignee details needed for the label. WhatsApp messages go only to merchants who opted in. Weight photos are kept for the dispute window in the merchant contract and then deleted. Branch staff see only their own branch's bookings.

What we deliver

  • WhatsApp booking Flow and portal booking form
  • Serviceability and restricted-item checks
  • Pickup slot assignment and reminder templates
  • Weight discrepancy evidence log

How we measure it

  • Pickups completed in the booked slot
  • Missed pickups per thousand bookings
  • Bookings received digitally
  • Weight dispute rate

Vehicle & driver assignmentStandard4–6 weeks

Driver and rider onboarding with document expiry alerts

Collect and verify driver and rider documents at onboarding, track every expiry date for licenses, registration, insurance, PUC, fitness and permits, and stop a vehicle or driver with a lapsed document from being assigned.

Fleet & road transport · Courier & last-mile delivery

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Licenses, registration certificates, insurance, PUC certificates, fitness certificates and permits expire on different dates and sit in folders, WhatsApp photos and spreadsheets. Lapses come to light at a checkpoint, during an accident claim or in a client audit. Courier networks onboarding many riders, including riders on their own two-wheelers, face the same problem at higher volume.

Trigger

A new driver or rider applies, a vehicle is added to the fleet, a document enters its reminder window before expiry, or a trip assignment is about to be confirmed.

How it runs

  • Collect documents through a WhatsApp Flow or onboarding form after a clear notice and consent, accepting DigiLocker-issued copies the applicant chooses to share.
  • Use OCR and an AI model to read names, numbers and expiry dates, and check license and registration details against VAHAN and SARATHI records through ULIP or an authorized verification provider.
  • Store each document with its expiry date in a compliance register per driver and vehicle, and flag mismatches such as a license class that does not cover the vehicle type.
  • Remind the driver, the vehicle owner and the fleet manager at agreed intervals before each expiry, and collect the renewed document in the same chat.
  • Check validity at trip assignment and hold confirmation of any driver or vehicle with a lapsed document until the fleet manager clears it.
  • Report upcoming expiries, lapses and renewals by branch, vendor and vehicle type.

Human checkpoint

The fleet or HR manager approves every onboarding after reviewing flagged mismatches, and decides any exception to the assignment hold. Background verification results are reviewed by a person; the AI model only reads and compares documents.

  • DigiLocker

Driver and rider documents are personal data. We collect only what the role and the law require, with a clear notice and consent, keep documents encrypted with access limited to HR and fleet managers, and do not store full Aadhaar numbers. Documents of drivers and riders who leave are deleted after the agreed retention period.

What we deliver

  • Validity check at trip assignment

How we measure it

  • Onboarding time from application to approval
  • Renewals completed before expiry
  • Assignments held for lapsed documents

In transit, at hubs & at customsAdvanced6–8 weeks

Proactive delay and SLA breach alerts with customer updates

Watch every shipment and warehouse order against its promised date or SLA, flag delays, stuck consignments, missed cut-offs and free-time risks early, give each exception an owner, and tell the customer before they have to ask.

Courier & last-mile delivery · Freight forwarding & customs · Warehousing & 3PL · Fleet & road transport

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Tracking data exists in the TMS, carrier portals, GPS dashboards and the WMS, but nobody watches all of it against what was promised. Delays surface when the customer calls, key accounts hear about rollovers or breakdowns late, warehouse orders miss the carrier cut-off unnoticed, and the same lanes, hubs and carriers fail repeatedly without data to show it.

Trigger

A milestone is missed or late against plan, the ETA moves past the promised date, a shipment shows no scan or GPS movement beyond the agreed limit, or an SLA timer nears breach.

How it runs

  • Pull milestones from the TMS, courier and carrier tracking APIs, GPS platforms, WMS order status and shipping line or airline feeds into one timeline with the promised date and SLA.
  • Run rules for missed pickups, no-movement, stuck-at-hub, ETA slippage, vessel rollovers, free-time expiry and warehouse orders not packed before the carrier cut-off, tuned per lane, service and client.
  • Create an exception with an owner, reason code and deadline in the control-tower queue, and alert the owner in Slack.
  • Send the consignee or shipper an approved WhatsApp, SMS or email update with the revised ETA; for key accounts, the account manager approves the message first.
  • Escalate exceptions still open near the SLA limit to the branch or operations head.
  • Report exceptions, causes and SLA performance by lane, hub, carrier and client for the weekly review.

Human checkpoint

Control-tower executives own every exception, confirm the reason before messages go to key accounts, and decide rerouting, upgrades and any cost or claim commitment. Customers are never promised compensation by an automated message.

In transit, at hubs & at customsAdvanced5–7 weeks

Tracking-grounded support assistant on WhatsApp and web

Answer where-is-my-shipment, delivery slot, document and stock questions on WhatsApp and web chat from live tracking and WMS data, and hand over to an agent with full context whenever a person is needed.

Courier & last-mile delivery · Freight forwarding & customs · Warehousing & 3PL

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Support teams spend much of the day reading tracking screens back to customers. Consignees ask about deliveries, importers about clearance and 3PL clients about receipts and orders. After hours nobody answers, and general chatbots that guess instead of checking the data create more calls than they save.

Trigger

A consignee, shipper or client sends a message on WhatsApp or web chat, or replies to a tracking notification.

How it runs

  • Identify the shipment or order from the AWB, booking, container or order number, and verify the requester through the registered phone number or a one-time code before sharing details.
  • Retrieve live status from the TMS, tracking APIs or WMS, and answer only from that data and the approved FAQ and service policies.
  • Handle routine requests such as a delivery slot, an address landmark or a document copy within the rules set for each customer.
  • Hand over to an agent with the conversation, shipment data and a suggested next step when the request involves a claim, damage, a refund, an address change outside the rules or an unhappy customer.
  • Log every conversation with intent and outcome, and review a weekly sample of answers for accuracy.

Human checkpoint

Support agents handle claims, damage reports, refunds, complaints and any change to delivery terms. The assistant states only what the data shows, says so when it does not know, and sends low-confidence answers to an agent.

Delivery, NDR & proof of deliveryStandard4–6 weeks

NDR resolution with consignee re-attempt choices

When a delivery fails, confirm the reason with the consignee, offer a re-attempt date, landmark, alternate contact or self-pickup, write the choice back to the courier platform before the next dispatch plan, and flag questionable attempts for review.

Courier & last-mile delivery

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Failed deliveries come back with codes such as consignee not available, refused or address incomplete, and some are recorded without a real attempt. Merchants chase consignees by phone, re-attempt instructions arrive after the rider has left, and shipments that could have been delivered become return-to-origin costs for the merchant and the courier.

Trigger

The rider app records a failed attempt with an NDR reason code, or a consignee replies to an out-for-delivery message to say they will not be available.

How it runs

  • Read the NDR event with reason code, attempt time, rider GPS position and call log from the courier platform.
  • Send the consignee an approved WhatsApp template where opt-in exists, or a DLT-registered SMS, confirming the attempt and offering a re-attempt date, landmark, alternate contact, pickup point or cancellation.
  • Capture the reply through quick-reply buttons; an AI model classifies free-text replies, and unclear ones go to an NDR agent.
  • Write the instruction back to the courier platform before the next dispatch planning cut-off, and update the merchant through the portal or API.
  • Flag attempts where the consignee disputes the reason, the rider's GPS position was far from the address or no call was placed, and send them to the hub supervisor.
  • Mark shipments for return to origin only after the agreed number of attempts or on the merchant's instruction.

Human checkpoint

NDR agents handle unclear replies and disputes, hub supervisors review flagged attempts and rider conduct, and the merchant decides returns for COD and high-value shipments. Address changes to another city or pin code need the merchant's approval.

Tools

Systems it connects

Consignee names, phone numbers and addresses are used only to complete the delivery and are masked from riders and agents where the platform allows. WhatsApp is used only with a valid opt-in, such as a checkout opt-in that names the courier, or from the merchant's own account, and messages carry no promotions. Reply logs are kept for the merchant dispute window and then deleted.

  • NDR and RTO dashboard by hub and merchant

How we measure it

  • First-attempt delivery rate
  • NDRs resolved by the next attempt
  • Return-to-origin rate
  • Disputed failure reasons

Billing, settlement & reviewStandard4–6 weeks

COD cash and remittance reconciliation

Reconcile cash-on-delivery collections from rider cash, UPI and card payments at the doorstep against delivered AWBs, flag short deposits and mismatches daily, and prepare merchant remittance files and statements for finance to release.

Courier & last-mile delivery

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

COD money moves through riders, branch cash, bank deposits, UPI collections and payment gateways before it reaches the merchant. Finance reconciles by AWB in spreadsheets, short deposits and duplicate entries surface weeks later, and merchants chase remittances and dispute deductions because statements do not tie back to their orders.

Trigger

The daily delivery and collection export closes, a branch records a cash deposit, a bank or payment gateway settlement arrives, or a merchant remittance cycle falls due.

How it runs

  • Pull delivered COD AWBs, rider cash collections, branch deposit records, bank statements and UPI or card settlement reports into one daily dataset.
  • Match collections to AWBs and deposits to collections, and flag short or late deposits by rider and branch, duplicate payments and delivered COD shipments with no collection.
  • Send branch managers a daily list of open mismatches with rider names and amounts, and track each to resolution.
  • Build merchant remittance files for each cycle with AWB-level detail and freight and RTO deductions, and record the bank UTR against each remittance once finance releases it.
  • Send merchants a statement with each remittance and route their disputes to the finance owner.

Human checkpoint

The finance controller approves every remittance batch before payment. Short deposits and suspected cash misuse are investigated by the branch manager and HR, never acted on by the automation, and disputed merchant deductions are held until a person decides.

Systems it connects

  • Rider cash deposit records
  • Bank statements and payment gateway settlements
  • UPI collection reports

Data & consent

Financial data about merchants and named riders, so access is limited to finance, branch managers and each merchant's own statements. Bank and gateway connections are read-only, with credentials in a secrets vault. Records follow accounting retention requirements, and rider-level discrepancy data is shared only with the people investigating it.

What we deliver

  • Daily COD reconciliation model
  • Branch and rider mismatch lists
  • Merchant remittance files and statements
  • COD aging and dispute dashboard

How we measure it

  • COD reconciliation lag
  • Unreconciled COD value by aging
  • Remittances paid on the agreed cycle
  • Merchant remittance disputes
